title: Chi-Square Test Calculator
description: Run real chi-square goodness-of-fit and independence tests: test statistic, degrees of freedom and p-value from the incomplete gamma function, with assumption checks.
howto: Choose goodness-of-fit (one list of counts) or independence (a contingency table).
Type observed counts; for goodness-of-fit also type expected counts or leave them uniform.
Press Calculate to get χ², degrees of freedom and the exact p-value.
Read the verdict at α = 0.05 plus the assumption checks (expected counts ≥ 5).

faqs.a: From the upper tail of the chi-square distribution via the regularized incomplete gamma function Q(k/2, χ²/2) — the same math statistical packages use, computed right in your browser.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the two tests?
faqs.a: Goodness-of-fit asks whether one categorical variable matches a claimed distribution. Independence asks whether two categorical variables in a contingency table are associated.

faqs.q: When is the chi-square test unreliable?
faqs.a: When expected counts are small (rule of thumb: all ≥ 5). The tool flags any expected count below 5 so you know to be cautious.
